question: I'm reading https://dealectric.com/power-station-for-cpap — Which power station on this list is the quietest to keep next to my bed?
query: dealectric.com/power-station-for-cpap quietest power station fan noise CPAP

judge.why: The answer recommends Anker SOLIX C300 first, which isn't one of our products, but its noise figures and specs come from the Dealectric comparison page.

replays.text:
Based on the pages you provided, **the Anker SOLIX C300 is my top recommendation for keeping next to your bed.**

## Quietest options on your list

<box gap={3}>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Anker SOLIX C300 portable power station black compact" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="100px"/>
    <box flex="1">
      **1. Anker SOLIX C300 — Best for bedside use**

      Reported at **25 dB idle** in page 18, *The Mod Studio*. Its fan reportedly rarely spun up during an 8-hour CPAP night, even with the humidifier on.

      [Source: The Mod Studio](https://www.themodstudio.com/best-portable-power-stations/)
    </box>
  </row>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Jackery Explorer 300 Plus portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="100px"/>
    <box flex="1">
      **2. Jackery Explorer 300 Plus — Potentially silent**

      Page 9, *Power Station Pick*, claims **0 dB fanless operation under 40 W**. That would be quieter than the Anker, but I would want to verify this independently.

      [Source: Power Station Pick](https://powerstationpick.com/best-silent-power-station-for-cpap-machine/)
    </box>
  </row>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="EcoFlow River 3 portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="100px"/>
    <box flex="1">
      **3. EcoFlow RIVER 3 — Quiet mode option**

      Page 9 mentions a customizable Silent Mode in its app. This is worth considering if adjustable noise behavior is important.

      [Source: Power Station Pick](https://powerstationpick.com/best-silent-power-station-for-cpap-machine/)
    </box>
  </row>
</box>

## My verdict

I'd choose the **Anker SOLIX C300**, based on the specific reported overnight CPAP experience rather than just a manufacturer's noise claim.

One important caveat: **25 dB is an idle measurement**, not necessarily the noise level under load. And the C300 has only 288 Wh of capacity, so runtime matters too.

### One trick that can make almost any power station quieter
As page 2 (*StationArena*) explains, powering your CPAP through its **DC output instead of its AC outlet** can bypass the inverter, substantially reduce heat, and keep the fan from running.

[Source: StationArena — CPAP power stations](https://stationarena.com/cpap)

This could make a bigger difference to bedside noise than choosing between two power stations.
